question: Does an in-game RPG hit on a tank's rear read 500 (registry Damage 125) or 540 (the asset's own 135)?

sourceFacts.method: The user reported one in-game reading. It was compared with the L3323 rule evaluated twice: with the registry default of the RPG's Damage and with the asset's own value (Field_91bb7b5f, named Damage in L3200). The grid value 2 for the RPG's material against the tank target and the top factor 2 are from L3323 and L3324.

control.description: In-game reading 500 for an RPG hit on a tank's rear, reported by the user on 9 October 2026.

reading.statement: tank rear hit from rpg is 500dmg
notRecorded: game build at the time of the reading (taken as the current live build)
tank type and its health before the hit

inference: The reading equals the registry prediction (125 x 2 x 2 = 500) and not the asset prediction (135 x 2 x 2 = 540). This is the first in-game reading for a disputed property and it follows the registry default.
It also equals the top of EA's 1.3.3.0 range for the RPG (188 to 500), so a rear hit takes the top hit-quality factor 2.
One user-reported reading, without a recording and without the conditions listed under notRecorded; it supports the registry rule and the damage rule, it does not prove them for other weapons.
unresolved: The reading's conditions are not recorded. Test: repeat the rear hit on a full-health main battle tank at about 20 m in a private match, record it, and note the build.
Front and side values. Test: the same RPG on the tank's front and side; 188 is the stored low end.
Other disputed pairs. Test: one M15 mine under a full-health tank, 390 (registry) or 600 (own).
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.
